title: Personal Checking: paying, returning and charging for items that would overdraw the account
content:
## Scope

This policy governs what happens on a Personal Checking account when a debit item would take the ledger balance below zero: whether the item is paid into overdraft, returned or declined, and which overdraft-item or returned-item fee follows. Coverage availability, coverage limit, fee amounts, de minimis amounts and the daily fee limit are each tier's own published figures.

## Formal clauses

1. **Posting order.** Within a business day all credits post first, then debit items in ascending order of amount, with checks of equal amount in ascending check number order.
2. **Transfer first.** When a debit item would take the ledger balance below zero, an overdraft protection transfer is attempted first. If no transfer covers the item, the tier decides.
3. **Tier without coverage.** When the tier does not offer discretionary overdraft coverage, ATM and debit card items are declined and nothing is recorded, and checks and ACH debits are returned unpaid as returned items.
4. **Tier with coverage, ATM and one-time card items.** An ATM withdrawal or one-time debit card purchase is paid into overdraft only if the account's debit overdraft election is opted in; otherwise it is declined with nothing recorded and no fee. The election is read from the account record.
5. **Tier with coverage, other items.** Checks, ACH debits and recurring debit card payments are paid into overdraft when the resulting negative ledger balance is no deeper than the tier's coverage limit, and otherwise returned unpaid.
6. **Fees.** Each item paid into overdraft incurs the tier's overdraft fee per item, tied to that debit. Each returned item incurs the tier's returned item fee, tied to the returned item.
7. **Small item.** No overdraft fee is charged on an item whose amount is the tier's per-item de minimis amount or less.
8. **Small end-of-day balance.** No overdraft or returned-item fee is charged for a business day whose end-of-day ledger balance is negative by the tier's end-of-day de minimis amount or less.
9. **Daily limit.** Overdraft-item and returned-item fees together are limited to the tier's daily combined limit per account per business day, counted in posting order; items beyond the limit carry no fee.
10. **Zero fee.** A tier fee of 0.00 means no fee is recorded.
11. **Status.** These fees are assessed only on an account whose status is active.
12. **One fee per item.** Each item can carry at most one overdraft-item or returned-item fee.
13. **Never charged on.** Fees never apply to credits, to the bank's own fee postings, or to items on a restricted account, where every debit that would overdraw is returned without a fee.

## Decision path for one debit that would overdraw (after the transfer attempt fails)

| Tier offers coverage | Item type | Further condition | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| No | ATM or debit card | — | Declined, nothing recorded |
| No | Check or ACH debit | — | Returned unpaid |
| Yes | ATM withdrawal or one-time debit card purchase | Election opted in | Paid into overdraft |
| Yes | ATM withdrawal or one-time debit card purchase | Election opted out | Declined, nothing recorded, no fee |
| Yes | Check, ACH debit or recurring debit card payment | Resulting negative balance no deeper than the coverage limit | Paid into overdraft |
| Yes | Check, ACH debit or recurring debit card payment | Resulting negative balance deeper than the coverage limit | Returned unpaid |

## Worked posting order (hypothetical business day)

Items presented on one day: a 40.00 USD deposit, a 75.00 USD ACH debit, check number 1002 for 20.00 USD and check number 1001 for 20.00 USD. The deposit posts first; then check 1001, then check 1002 (equal amounts, ascending check number), then the 75.00 ACH debit (larger amount last).

## Points of judgement

- **Wrong reading:** "an opted-out customer's check is also declined". **Correct basis:** the election governs only ATM withdrawals and one-time debit card purchases.
- **Wrong reading:** "a restricted account pays an overdraft fee for each returned item". **Correct basis:** on a restricted account every debit that would overdraw is returned without a fee.
